description: Free 0-100 score of how easily AI assistants and agents can read, quote and contact a public business website: AI crawler rules, llms.txt, schema.org business/offer data, agent catalog, MCP card, sitemap, meta, contact. Not a Google ranking score.
name: agent_readiness_score
title: Agent-Readiness Score (free)

description: Generate robots.txt AI-crawler rules, llms.txt, schema.org JSON-LD and /.well-known/agent-catalog.json from facts the business supplies. services: one per line as "Name|Price". Uses only supplied facts.
name: agent_ready_fix_pack
title: Agent-Ready fix pack generator (free)

description: Check a public site robots.txt for AI crawler allow/deny verdicts.

path.description: Optional path to test against the rules, default /

url.description: Public site URL or domain, e.g. https://example.com

name: ai_crawler_audit
title: AI crawler robots.txt audit

description: Room air-conditioner capacity using the ENERGY STAR sizing chart and its adjustments for sun, occupants and kitchens. Formula: Base BTU from the ENERGY STAR area chart; −10% heavily shaded, +10% very sunny, +600 BTU per person above 2, +4,000 BTU for a kitchen.

kitchen.description: Used as kitchen; default 0; one of 0 = No, 1 = Yes (+4,000 BTU)

name: calc_ac_btu
title: Room AC BTU Calculator (ENERGY STAR Sizing)

description: Daily and yearly kWh and the cost to run any appliance from its wattage, hours of use and your electricity rate. Formula: kWh per day = watts × hours ÷ 1,000; kWh per year = kWh per day × days; cost = kWh × rate.

rate_per_kwh.description: Your electricity rate (from your bill) ($/kWh); default 0.15

watts.description: Appliance wattage (nameplate, or amps × volts) (W); default 1500

name: calc_appliance_energy_cost
title: Appliance Energy Cost Calculator (kWh and $ per Year)

description: Tons of hot-mix asphalt for a driveway or lot from area, compacted depth and mix density. Formula: Tons = L × W × depth(in)/12 × density(lb/cu ft) ÷ 2,000.

lb_per_cf.description: Mix density (ask your plant) (lb/cu ft); default 145

name: calc_asphalt
title: Asphalt Calculator (Tons for Driveways)

description: How much attic ventilation you need by the 1/150 and 1/300 rules (Florida Building Code, Residential R806.2), split into intake and exhaust, and how many vents that is for your vent products. Formula: Total net free area (sq in) = attic floor area (sq ft) × 144 ÷ 150 (or ÷ 300 under the balanced exception). Exhaust NFA = total × high share; intake NFA = the rest. Vents = ⌈NFA ÷ the net free area of one vent (or one foot of continuous vent)⌉.

attic_floor_sqft.description: Attic floor area (vented space) (sq ft); default 1500

exhaust_nfa_per_unit.description: Exhaust vent net free area per unit or per ft of ridge vent (from the label) (sq in); default 18

intake_nfa_per_unit.description: Intake vent net free area per unit or per ft of soffit vent (from the label) (sq in); default 9

ratio.description: Ventilation rule; default 150; one of 150 = 1/150 (standard), 300 = 1/300 (balanced exception: 40–50% high)

upper_pct.description: Share of vent area that is high (exhaust) (%); default 50

name: calc_attic_ventilation
title: Attic Ventilation Calculator (Net Free Area, Ridge & Soffit Vents)

description: Board feet and cost for hardwood or dimensional lumber. Formula: Board feet = thickness(in) × width(in) × length(ft) ÷ 12 × pieces (one board foot = 144 cubic inches).

price_per_bf.description: Price per board foot (0 = skip) ($); default 0

name: calc_board_foot
title: Board Foot Calculator (Lumber)

description: Required box volume under NEC 314.16 from your conductors, devices, clamps, fittings and grounds, checked against a standard metal box from Table 314.16(A) or your box's marked volume. Formula: Required volume = Σ(conductors × Table 314.16(B) allowance) + 1 allowance for clamps + 1 per fitting type + 2 per yoke + 1 for all grounds, each at the largest conductor size present. Allowances: 18 AWG 1.50, 16 AWG 1.75, 14 AWG 2.00, 12 AWG 2.25, 10 AWG 2.50, 8 AWG 3.00, 6 AWG 5.00 cu in.

clamps.description: Internal cable clamps; default 0; one of 0 = None, 1 = Yes (one or more)

grounds.description: Equipment grounding conductors; default 1; one of 1 = Yes (one or more), 0 = None

name: calc_box_fill
title: Electrical Box Fill Calculator (NEC 314.16)

description: Bricks for a single-wythe wall from its area, the brick face size and the mortar joint. Defaults are a modular brick with a ⅜ in joint. Formula: Bricks per sq ft = 144 ÷ ((length + joint) × (height + joint)); bricks = (wall area − openings) × bricks per sq ft × (1 + waste%).
name: calc_brick
title: Brick Calculator (How Many Bricks for a Wall)

description: How many tubes of caulk or sealant to buy: linear feet per cartridge for your joint width and depth (or a triangular corner bead), and cartridges for the total length. Formula: Cartridge volume = fl oz × 1.80469 cu in. Bead area = width × depth (or leg² ÷ 2). Linear feet per cartridge = volume ÷ (bead area × 12). Cartridges = length × (1 + waste) ÷ feet per cartridge.
name: calc_caulk
title: Caulk Calculator (Tubes of Caulk or Sealant per Linear Foot)

description: What size ceiling fan you need for a room: the suggested blade span from the room's square footage, the largest fan that keeps 18 in from the walls, and the mount type for your ceiling height. Formula: Area = length × width. Blade span: up to 75 sq ft 29–36 in; 76–144 sq ft 36–42 in; 144–225 sq ft 44 in; 225–400 sq ft 50–54 in; over 400 sq ft 54–72 in or several fans. Largest span with 18 in wall clearance = shorter side (in) − 36 in. Mount: 8 ft or lower → hugger; 8–9 ft → standard downrod; higher → extended downrod.
name: calc_ceiling_fan_size
title: Ceiling Fan Size Calculator (Blade Span by Room Size)

description: Number of 8×8×16 concrete blocks (CMU) for a wall. A standard block plus a ⅜ in joint covers 16 × 8 in, so about 1.125 blocks per square foot. Formula: Blocks per sq ft = 144 ÷ ((length + joint) × (height + joint)) = 144 ÷ (16 × 8) = 1.125 for standard units; blocks = net wall area × 1.125 × (1 + waste%).
name: calc_concrete_block
title: Concrete Block (CMU) Calculator

description: Concrete needed for round columns, piers and tube forms (sonotubes). Uses cylinder volume, which differs from slab math. Formula: Cubic feet = π × (diameter(in)/24)² × height(ft) × count; cubic yards = cu ft ÷ 27 × (1 + waste%).
name: calc_concrete_column
title: Concrete Column & Sonotube Calculator

description: Volume for continuous trench/wall footings where width is in inches and length runs the full perimeter. Formula: Cubic yards = Length(ft) × Width(in)/12 × Depth(in)/12 ÷ 27 × (1 + waste%).
name: calc_concrete_footing
title: Concrete Footing Calculator (Continuous Wall Footings)

description: Estimate ready-mix cubic yards or the number of 80 lb bags for a rectangular slab, patio or driveway. Formula: Cubic yards = Length(ft) × Width(ft) × Thickness(in)/12 ÷ 27 × (1 + waste%). Bags = cubic feet ÷ bag yield.
name: calc_concrete_slab
title: Concrete Slab Calculator (Cubic Yards & Bags)

description: How much concrete solid steps need, from the total height to climb: number of risers, riser height, treads, top landing, cubic yards and 80 lb bags. Formula: Risers n = ⌈total rise ÷ max riser⌉; riser height R = total rise ÷ n. Side profile area = tread × R × n(n − 1) ÷ 2 + landing depth × n × R (each lower tread is a block of its own height; the landing sits at full height). Volume (cu ft) = profile (sq in) × width (in) ÷ 1,728; cubic yards = cu ft × (1 + waste) ÷ 27; bags = cu ft × (1 + waste) ÷ bag yield.

bag_yield_cf.description: Bag yield (from the bag) (cu ft/bag); default 0.6

landing_depth_in.description: Top landing depth (0 = no landing) (in); default 36

max_riser_in.description: Max riser height (IRC 7¾ in; check your local code) (in); default 7.75

total_rise_in.description: Total rise (ground to top of landing) (in); default 21

name: calc_concrete_steps
title: Concrete Steps Calculator (Cubic Yards, Bags, Risers & Landing)

description: Conduit fill for THHN/THWN-2 wires in EMT or Schedule 40 PVC: total wire area, percent fill against the NEC 53/31/40% limits, whether it fits, the smallest conduit that does, and the maximum number of same-size wires. Formula: Wire area = Σ count × Table 5 area (14 AWG 0.0097, 12 AWG 0.0133, 10 AWG 0.0211, 8 AWG 0.0366, 6 AWG 0.0507 sq in …). Allowed = Table 4 conduit area × 53% (1 wire), 31% (2) or 40% (3+). Same-size maximum = allowed ÷ wire area, rounded up only at 0.8 or more.
name: calc_conduit_fill
title: Conduit Fill Calculator (NEC Chapter 9, EMT and PVC)

description: Number of deck boards for a rectangular deck, accounting for board width and gap. Formula: Rows = ⌈width(in) ÷ (board width + gap)⌉; boards = rows × ⌈deck length ÷ board length⌉ × (1 + waste%).
name: calc_deck_board
title: Deck Board Calculator

description: What size portable dehumidifier you need, in pints per day, from the ENERGY STAR chart for your space size and how damp it is, with a liters and gallons conversion. Formula: Pick the ENERGY STAR range for the condition and size (under or over 2,000 sq ft), then take the top of the range, or the water your current unit removes per day if that is higher. Liters = pints × 0.4732; gallons = pints ÷ 8.

condition.description: Condition without a dehumidifier; default very

pints_emptied_per_day.description: Water you empty now, if replacing a unit (optional) (pints/day); default 0

name: calc_dehumidifier_size
title: Dehumidifier Size Calculator (Pints per Day by Room Size)

description: Number of drywall sheets for walls and optionally the ceiling. Formula: Sheets = (perimeter × height + ceiling area) × (1 + waste%) ÷ sheet area.

include_ceiling.description: Include ceiling; default 1; one of 1 = Yes, 0 = No

name: calc_drywall
title: Drywall Calculator (Sheets Needed)

description: How much epoxy floor coating to buy: coverage per gallon at your dry film thickness and volume solids, gallons per coat, total with losses, and kits. Formula: Coverage (sq ft/gal) = 1,604 × solids by volume ÷ dry mils. Gallons per coat = area ÷ coverage. Total = gallons per coat × coats × (1 + loss). Wet mils = dry mils ÷ solids.

dry_mils_per_coat.description: Dry film thickness per coat (from the data sheet) (mils); default 8

solids_pct.description: Solids by volume (from the data sheet) (%); default 100

name: calc_epoxy_floor
title: Epoxy Floor Calculator (Gallons and Kits by Mils and Solids)

description: What it costs to charge an electric car at home: cost per mile, per month and per full charge from your car's kWh per 100 miles and your state's average residential electricity price (EIA, August 2026) or your own rate, with an optional gas comparison. Formula: Cost per mile = kWh/100 mi ÷ 100 × $/kWh ÷ (1 − loss%). Month = cost per mile × miles. Full charge = battery kWh × $/kWh ÷ (1 − loss%). Gas cost per mile = $/gal ÷ mpg.

battery_kwh.description: Battery size (optional, for full-charge cost) (kWh); default 0

rate_per_kwh.description: Your rate (optional; overrides the state) ($/kWh); default 0

state.description: State (EIA average residential rate); default US

name: calc_ev_charging_cost
title: EV Charging Cost Calculator (Cost per Mile, Month and Full Charge by State)

description: Posts, rails and pickets for a straight run of wood privacy or picket fence. Formula: Sections = ⌈length ÷ spacing⌉; posts = sections + 1 + gates; pickets = ⌈length(in) ÷ (picket width + gap)⌉.
name: calc_fence
title: Fence Calculator (Posts, Rails & Pickets)

description: Square footage plus waste and number of boxes for tile, laminate, vinyl plank or hardwood. Formula: Area = L × W; to buy = area × (1 + waste%); boxes = to buy ÷ coverage per box.

box_coverage_sqft.description: Coverage per box (on the box) (sq ft); default 20

waste_pct.description: Waste allowance (more for diagonal layouts) (%); default 10

name: calc_flooring_tile
title: Flooring & Tile Calculator (Square Feet & Boxes)

description: What size generator you need for a power outage: add the running watts of everything you will run at once, then add the single biggest motor starting surge. Enter how many of each item you plan to run at the same time. Formula: Total running watts = Σ (quantity × running watts). Total starting watts = total running watts + the single highest additional starting watts among the items you run, because motors rarely start at the same instant. Amps at 240 V = running watts ÷ 240. Margin is an optional buffer you choose.

box_fan.description: Box fan, 20 in: how many (200 W running); default 0

central_ac_24k.description: Central AC, 24,000 BTU (2 ton): how many (3,800 W running, +4,950 W to start); default 0

central_ac_40k.description: Central AC, 40,000 BTU: how many (6,000 W running, +6,700 W to start); default 0

coffee_maker.description: Coffee maker: how many (1,000 W running); default 0

electric_water_heater.description: Electric water heater: how many (4,000 W running); default 0

furnace_fan_half_hp.description: Furnace fan blower, 1/2 HP: how many (800 W running, +2,350 W to start); default 0

garage_door_half_hp.description: Garage door opener, 1/2 HP: how many (875 W running, +2,350 W to start); default 0

light_60w.description: Light bulb, 60 W: how many (60 W running); default 4

microwave_1000w.description: Microwave, 1,000 W: how many (1,000 W running); default 1

other_running_w.description: Other running watts (TV, router, chargers: from nameplates) (W); default 300

other_starting_w.description: Extra starting watts of your largest other motor (0 if none) (W); default 0

refrigerator.description: Refrigerator/freezer: how many (700 W running, +2,200 W to start); default 1

space_heater.description: Space heater: how many (1,800 W running); default 0

sump_pump_half_hp.description: Sump pump, 1/2 HP: how many (1,050 W running, +2,200 W to start); default 0

washing_machine.description: Washing machine: how many (1,150 W running, +2,250 W to start); default 0

well_pump_third_hp.description: Water well pump, 1/3 HP: how many (1,000 W running, +2,200 W to start); default 0

window_ac_10k.description: Window AC, 10,000 BTU: how many (1,200 W running, +1,800 W to start); default 1

name: calc_generator_size
title: Generator Size Calculator (Running & Starting Watts for Your House)

description: How much grass seed to buy for a new lawn: university seeding rates per 1,000 sq ft for each grass type or mix, adjusted for the purity and germination printed on the seed tag. Formula: Pure live seed (PLS) = purity × germination. Seed (lb) = rate (lb PLS per 1,000 sq ft) × area ÷ 1,000 ÷ PLS. Bags = high-rate pounds ÷ bag size, rounded up.
name: calc_grass_seed
title: Grass Seed Calculator (Pounds of Seed for a New Lawn)

description: How much grout a tile job takes from the tile size, joint width, joint depth and area, in pounds and bags. The grout density is editable so you can match your product. Formula: Each tile plus its joint is a (L + J) × (W + J) module, of which J × (L + W + J) is joint. Joint share = J(L + W + J) ÷ ((L + J)(W + J)). Grout volume (cu ft) = area × joint share × depth(in) ÷ 12; pounds = volume × density × (1 + waste); bags = ⌈pounds ÷ bag size⌉.

density_lb_cf.description: Grout weight per cubic foot of joint (from your grout data sheet; ~100 sanded, ~85 unsanded) (lb/cu ft); default 100

name: calc_grout
title: Tile Grout Calculator (Pounds and Bags of Grout)

description: Check whether a gutter can carry the runoff from your roof in a design storm, and how many downspouts it needs. Uses the USDA NRCS gutter and downspout capacity table and your local rainfall intensity. Formula: Runoff Q (cfs) = roof area (sq ft) × rainfall intensity (in/hr) ÷ 43,200 (12 in/ft × 3,600 s/hr); gpm = cfs × 448.8. The gutter is adequate when Q ≤ its NRCS PA-1 capacity at your slope. Downspouts = the larger of ⌈Q ÷ one downspout's PA-1 capacity⌉ and ⌈run length ÷ max length per downspout⌉. Max roof area for the gutter = capacity × 43,200 ÷ intensity.

max_run_per_downspout_ft.description: Max gutter length per downspout (SMACNA practical max 50 ft) (ft); default 50

rain_in_per_hr.description: Design rainfall intensity (5-minute depth from NOAA Atlas 14 × 12) (in/hr); default 6

roof_area_sqft.description: Roof area draining to this gutter (plan view, not slope length) (sq ft); default 1200

name: calc_gutter_size
title: Gutter & Downspout Size Calculator (Roof Runoff, Gutter Capacity, Number of Downspouts)

description: Thickness needed to reach a target R-value for the R-per-inch printed on your insulation product. Formula: Thickness(in) = target R ÷ R per inch. Volume in board feet = area(sq ft) × thickness(in).
name: calc_insulation_r_value
title: Insulation R-Value Thickness Calculator

description: How much drywall mud and tape to buy: gallons of ready-mix joint compound, 4.5 gal pails and rolls of paper tape for your square footage of drywall, using USG's published coverage. Formula: Gallons = area × coverage ÷ 1,000 × (1 + waste). Pails = gallons ÷ pail size, rounded up. Tape (ft) = area × 370 ÷ 1,000 × (1 + waste). Rolls = tape ÷ roll length, rounded up.

coverage_gal_per_1000.description: Compound coverage (from the label) (gal per 1,000 sq ft); default 10

tape_ft_per_1000.description: Tape coverage (ft per 1,000 sq ft); default 370

name: calc_joint_compound
title: Joint Compound Calculator (Drywall Mud & Tape)

description: How much fertilizer to put on your lawn: pounds of product per 1,000 sq ft and for the whole lawn, from the nitrogen rate you want and the N-P-K numbers on the bag, plus bags to buy and the phosphate and potash you apply along with it. Formula: Product per 1,000 sq ft = N rate ÷ (N% ÷ 100). Total = product per 1,000 × area ÷ 1,000. Bags = total ÷ bag weight, rounded up. P₂O₅ (or K₂O) per 1,000 = product per 1,000 × P% (or K%) ÷ 100.

n_lb_per_1000.description: Nitrogen rate wanted (lb N per 1,000 sq ft); default 1

n_pct.description: Nitrogen % (first number on the bag); default 24

name: calc_lawn_fertilizer
title: Lawn Fertilizer Calculator (Pounds per 1,000 Sq Ft from N-P-K)

description: Mortar for a brick or concrete block wall: units needed, cubic feet of mortar from the Brick Industry Association quantity table (with bond-pattern correction and waste) and bags of mason mix. Formula: Brick = wall ÷ 100 × Table 4 brick per 100 sq ft × (1 + bond brick factor). Mortar (cu ft) = brick ÷ 1,000 × Table 4 cu ft per 1,000 brick for the joint × (1 + bond mortar factor) × (1 + waste). Block = wall × 1.125. Bags = units ÷ units per bag × (1 + waste).

joint_in.description: Mortar joint (brick); default 0.375; one of 0.375 = 3/8 in, 0.5 = 1/2 in

units_per_bag.description: Units per 80 lb bag (0 = 37 brick / 13 block); default 0

name: calc_mortar
title: Mortar Calculator for Brick and Block (Cubic Feet & Bags)

description: Cubic yards (and optional tons) of mulch, gravel, sand or soil for a bed or path. Formula: Cubic yards = L(ft) × W(ft) × depth(in) ÷ 324 (since 27 cu ft × 12 in = 324). Tons = cu yd × supplier density.

tons_per_cy.description: Material density from your supplier (0 = skip) (tons/cu yd); default 0

name: calc_mulch_gravel
title: Mulch, Gravel & Topsoil Calculator (Cubic Yards)

description: Gallons in an oval (elliptical) pool. Formula: Gallons = π × (L/2) × (W/2) × average depth × 7.48052.
name: calc_oval_pool_volume
title: Pool Volume Calculator: Oval (Gallons)

description: Gallons of wall paint from room perimeter and height, minus doors and windows, for any number of coats. Formula: Paintable area = perimeter × height − 20 sq ft per door − 15 sq ft per window. Gallons = area × coats ÷ label coverage.

coverage_sqft_per_gal.description: Coverage (from your can label) (sq ft/gal); default 350

name: calc_paint
title: Paint Calculator (Gallons for Walls)

description: Number of pavers for a patio, walkway or driveway plus cubic yards of compacted base and bedding sand. Formula: Pavers per sq ft = 144 ÷ (paver length × width); pavers = area × per sq ft × (1 + waste%). Base and sand cubic yards = area × depth(in) ÷ 324.
name: calc_paver
title: Paver Calculator (Pavers, Base Gravel & Sand)

description: How much baking soda raises your pool's total alkalinity, or how much muriatic acid or dry acid lowers it, for your pool size, using published doses per 10,000 gallons. Formula: Batches = |target − current| ÷ 10 × gallons ÷ 10,000. Raise: baking soda (lb) = batches × 1.4. Lower: muriatic acid 31.4% (fl oz) = batches × 26, or sodium bisulfate (lb) = batches × 2.1. Additions: raise no more than about 50 ppm at a time; add no more than 1 quart of acid per 10,000 gallons at a time.

target_ppm.description: Target total alkalinity (from your pool builder or test kit guide) (ppm); default 100

name: calc_pool_alkalinity
title: Pool Alkalinity Calculator (Baking Soda to Raise, Muriatic Acid to Lower)

description: How much calcium chloride raises your pool's calcium hardness, or how much water to replace to lower it, based on your pool size and fill-water hardness. Formula: Raise: calcium chloride (lb) = (target − current) ÷ 10 × gallons ÷ 10,000 × 1.2 for 77% (0.9 for 100%). Lower (dilution): share to drain = (current − target) ÷ (current − fill water); gallons = share × pool volume.

fill_water_ppm.description: Calcium hardness of your fill water (ppm); default 50

product.description: Calcium chloride strength (on the label); default 77; one of 77 = 77% (flake / dihydrate), 100 = 100% (anhydrous)

target_ppm.description: Target calcium hardness (from your pool builder or test kit guide) (ppm); default 250

name: calc_pool_calcium_hardness
title: Pool Calcium Hardness Calculator (Calcium Chloride to Raise, Water to Drain to Lower)

description: Fluid ounces of liquid chlorine (sodium hypochlorite) to raise free chlorine by a target number of ppm, from pool volume and product strength. Formula: Available chlorine (g) = gallons × 3.78541 L/gal × ppm (mg/L) ÷ 1,000. Product (mL) = grams ÷ (strength% ÷ 100), since trade percent is grams of available chlorine per 100 mL. Fl oz = mL ÷ 29.5735.

strength_pct.description: Product strength (trade %, on the jug) (%); default 12.5

name: calc_pool_chlorine
title: Pool Liquid Chlorine Calculator (Ounces to Raise Free Chlorine)

description: Heater output in Btu per hour for an outdoor pool from surface area and temperature rise, using the U.S. Department of Energy formula, plus gas input, the matching standard heat pump size and the time to warm the water. Formula: Temperature rise = desired pool temperature − average air temperature of the coldest month of use. Heater output (Btu/h) = surface area × rise × 12 × rate factor (1, 1.5 or 2). Gas input = output ÷ efficiency. Heat to warm the water once = gallons × 8.34 lb × (desired − starting temperature); hours = that ÷ output, with no losses.

coldest_air_f.description: Average air temperature, coldest month you swim (°F); default 65

heatup_rate.description: Heat-up rate; default 1; one of 1 = 1 to 1¼ °F per hour (DOE base), 1.5 = 1½ °F per hour (×1.5), 2 = 2 °F per hour (×2)

pool_gallons.description: Pool volume (optional, for warm-up time) (gal); default 22000

surface_sqft.description: Pool surface area (length × width for a rectangle) (sq ft); default 512

name: calc_pool_heater_size
title: Pool Heater Size Calculator (BTU for Gas Heaters and Heat Pumps)

description: Langelier Saturation Index for your pool or spa from pH, water temperature, calcium hardness and total alkalinity, using the factor table and formula in state pool rules, plus the pH that would balance it. Formula: SI = pH + TF + CF + AF − 12.1 (12.2 when TDS is above 1,000 ppm). TF, CF and AF come from the temperature, calcium hardness and alkalinity factor table; when a reading falls between rows the table method uses the next greater row. pH for SI = 0: 12.1 − TF − CF − AF.

tds_ppm.description: Total dissolved solids (0 if unknown) (ppm); default 0

name: calc_pool_lsi
title: Pool LSI Calculator (Langelier Saturation Index / Water Balance)

description: Pounds and bags of pool salt to raise a saltwater pool from its current salt level to the target your chlorine generator needs. Formula: Salt (lb) = gallons × 8.34 lb/gal × (target ppm − current ppm) ÷ 1,000,000. Bags = ⌈lb ÷ bag size⌉.

current_ppm.description: Current salt level (test strip or meter) (ppm); default 0

target_ppm.description: Target salt level (from your cell manual) (ppm); default 3200

name: calc_pool_salt
title: Pool Salt Calculator (Pounds of Salt for a Saltwater Pool)

description: How much stabilizer (cyanuric acid, CYA) raises your pool to a target level, or how much water to drain and refill to lower it. Formula: Raise: stabilizer (oz) = (target − current) ÷ 10 × gallons ÷ 10,000 × 13. Lower (dilution): share to drain = (current − target) ÷ (current − fill water); gallons = share × pool volume.

fill_water_ppm.description: Cyanuric acid in your fill water (ppm); default 0

target_ppm.description: Target cyanuric acid (from your pool builder or test kit guide) (ppm); default 40

name: calc_pool_stabilizer
title: Pool Stabilizer (Cyanuric Acid) Calculator: How Much to Add or Drain

description: The flow rate (gpm) your pool pump must deliver for a target turnover time, your actual turnover from a flow meter reading, and whether your filter is big enough for that flow. Formula: Required flow (gpm) = gallons ÷ (turnover hours × 60). Actual turnover (hours) = gallons ÷ (measured gpm × 60). Filter max flow = filter area × rated gpm per sq ft.

filter_area_sqft.description: Filter area (from the filter label, 0 to skip) (sq ft); default 0

filter_rate_gpm_per_sqft.description: Max filter rate (from the filter label) (gpm/sq ft); default 0

measured_gpm.description: Flow meter reading (0 to skip) (gpm); default 60

name: calc_pool_turnover
title: Pool Turnover Rate & Pump GPM Calculator

description: Gallons in a rectangular pool with a sloped bottom, using average depth. Formula: Gallons = L × W × (shallow + deep)/2 × 7.48052 gal/cu ft.
name: calc_pool_volume
title: Pool Volume Calculator: Rectangular (Swimming Pool Gallons)

description: Common rafter length, ridge rise and roof angle from the horizontal run and pitch, with optional overhang. Formula: Pitch factor = √(1 + (rise/12)²). Rafter length = (run + overhang) × pitch factor. Ridge rise = run × rise ÷ 12. Angle = atan(rise ÷ 12).

pitch_rise.description: Pitch (rise per 12 in of run) (in); default 6

run_ft.description: Horizontal run (half the span, minus half the ridge board) (ft); default 14

name: calc_rafter_length
title: Rafter Length Calculator (From Run and Roof Pitch)

description: How many gallons of rainwater your roof can collect from a storm, a month or a year of rain, how many rain barrels that fills, and how much to divert as first flush, using the Texas Manual on Rainwater Harvesting method. Formula: Gallons = rainfall (in) × roof footprint (sq ft) × 0.62 × efficiency. Barrels = gallons ÷ barrel size, rounded up. First flush = roof ÷ 1,000 × 10 gal.

first_flush_gal_per_1000.description: First-flush diversion (gal per 1,000 sq ft); default 10

name: calc_rainwater_harvesting
title: Rainwater Harvesting Calculator (Gallons from Your Roof)

description: How much rebar a rectangular slab grid needs: bar count each way, lap splices, total linear feet, 20 ft sticks to order and steel weight from ASTM A615 bar weights. Formula: Bars each way = ⌊(clear span ÷ spacing)⌋ + 1, where clear span = side × 12 − 2 × edge clearance. A run longer than one stick needs ⌈(run − lap) ÷ (stick − lap)⌉ pieces, adding one lap per joint; lap = bar diameters × bar diameter. Linear ft = (bars × run + splices × lap) ÷ 12; sticks = ⌈linear ft × (1 + allowance) ÷ stick length⌉; weight = linear ft × ASTM A615 lb/ft.

lap_bar_diameters.description: Lap splice length in bar diameters (from your plans or engineer); default 40

spacing_in.description: Bar spacing on center (from your plans) (in); default 12

name: calc_rebar
title: Rebar Calculator for a Slab (Bars, Sticks, Lap Splices & Weight)

description: How many retaining wall blocks you need for a straight wall or a circle (fire pit, tree ring), including the buried course, cap units, base gravel for the leveling pad and drainage rock behind the wall. Block sizes are editable because every product line differs. Formula: Buried depth = max(exposed height ÷ bury ratio, minimum). Courses = ⌈(exposed height + buried depth − cap height) ÷ block height⌉. Blocks per course = ⌈run ÷ block face length⌉, where run = wall length, or π × outside diameter for a circle. Wall blocks = ⌈blocks per course × courses × (1 + waste%)⌉; caps = ⌈run ÷ cap length × (1 + waste%)⌉. Base gravel cu yd = run(ft) × trench width(in) × base depth(in) ÷ 144 ÷ 27; drainage rock cu yd = run(ft) × zone depth(in) × stacked block height(in) ÷ 144 ÷ 27 (straight walls only).

block_height_in.description: Block height (from the block label) (in); default 4

block_length_in.description: Block face length (from the block label) (in); default 12

bury_ratio_in.description: Bury 1 in of block for every __ in of exposed height (from your block maker) (in); default 8

drain_zone_in.description: Drainage rock zone behind the block (in); default 12

exposed_height_in.description: Exposed wall height above grade (including cap) (in); default 24

length_or_diameter_ft.description: Wall length (straight) or outside diameter (circle) (ft); default 20

min_bury_in.description: Minimum buried depth (from your block maker) (in); default 6

name: calc_retaining_wall
title: Retaining Wall Block Calculator (Blocks, Caps, Base Gravel & Drainage Rock)

description: Roof area from the house footprint and pitch, converted to roofing squares (100 sq ft) and shingle bundles. Formula: Pitch factor = √(1 + (rise/12)²). Roof area = (L + 2×overhang) × (W + 2×overhang) × pitch factor. Squares = area ÷ 100 × (1 + waste%).
name: calc_roofing
title: Roofing Calculator (Squares, Bundles & Pitch Factor)

description: Gallons in a round or above-ground pool. Formula: Gallons = π × (D/2)² × average depth × 7.48052 (≈ D² × depth × 5.875).
name: calc_round_pool_volume
title: Pool Volume Calculator: Round / Above-Ground (Gallons)

description: How many bags of self-leveling underlayment or floor resurfacer to buy, from your floor area and the thinnest and thickest pour depth, using the bag's yield in cubic feet. Formula: Average depth = (thinnest + thickest) ÷ 2. Volume = area × average depth ÷ 12. Bags = volume × (1 + allowance) ÷ yield per bag. Coverage at 1/4 in = yield ÷ (0.25 ÷ 12).

bag_yield_cuft.description: Yield per bag (from the bag or data sheet) (cu ft); default 0.45

name: calc_self_leveling_concrete
title: Self-Leveling Concrete Calculator (Bags of Floor Leveler)

description: Minimum septic tank size, pump tank size and drainfield area for a single-family home under Florida Rule 62-6.008, from bedrooms, building area and soil type. Formula: Design flow = the larger of the bedroom flow (100 gpd per bedroom up to 4, then +60 per bedroom) and the building-area flow (100 gpd to 750 sq ft, 200 to 1,200, 300 to 2,250, 400 to 3,300, then +60 per extra 750 sq ft or fraction), per Table I and its footnote 4. Septic tank and pump tank minimums come from Table II for that flow. Drainfield area = max(flow, 200 gpd) ÷ the Table III loading rate for the soil and trench or bed.

soil.description: Soil (from the site evaluation); default slight

name: calc_septic_tank_size
title: Septic Tank Size Calculator (Florida Rule 62-6.008: Tank Gallons & Drainfield Area)

description: Square feet of sod, number of pieces and pallets for a lawn area. Piece size and pallet coverage are editable because they vary by farm and grass type. Formula: Sq ft to buy = L × W × (1 + waste%); pieces = sq ft ÷ (piece length × width ÷ 144); pallets = sq ft ÷ pallet coverage.

pallet_sqft.description: Coverage per pallet (ask your supplier) (sq ft); default 400

name: calc_sod
title: Sod Calculator (Square Feet, Pieces & Pallets)

description: Panels needed to offset annual electricity use, from panel wattage, peak sun hours and system losses. Formula: Annual kWh per panel = W/1000 × peak sun hours × 365 × (1 − losses). Panels = ⌈annual use ÷ kWh per panel⌉.

peak_sun_hours.description: Peak sun hours/day (look up in PVWatts) (h); default 5

name: calc_solar_panel
title: Solar Panel Calculator (How Many Panels Do I Need?)

description: Number of risers and treads, exact riser height, total run and stringer length from the floor-to-floor rise, checked against the IRC 7¾ in maximum riser. Formula: Risers = ⌈total rise ÷ max riser⌉; riser height = total rise ÷ risers; treads = risers − 1; total run = treads × tread depth; stringer length = √(rise² + run²).

total_rise_in.description: Total rise (finished floor to finished floor) (in); default 108

name: calc_stair_stringer
title: Stair Stringer Calculator (Risers, Treads & Stringer Length)

description: How many 80 lb bags of stucco you need for a wall: base coat (scratch and brown) bags from the manufacturer's coverage at your system thickness, plus finish coat bags. Formula: Area = (wall − openings) × (1 + waste). Base bags = area ÷ coverage, where coverage per 80 lb bag = 20–24 sq ft × (3/8 in ÷ base thickness). Finish bags = area ÷ (70 sq ft × 1/8 in ÷ finish thickness).

openings_sqft.description: Windows and doors to subtract (sq ft); default 100

name: calc_stucco
title: Stucco Calculator (Bags of Base and Finish Coat)

description: Size a tankless water heater from your peak hot-water flow and the rise from winter inlet temperature to your setpoint: required Btu/h, gas input, electric kW and amps. Formula: Temperature rise = setpoint − inlet. Heat output (Btu/h) = gpm × 8.34 lb/gal × 60 min × rise. Gas input = output ÷ efficiency. Electric kW = output ÷ 3,412.14; amps = kW × 1,000 ÷ volts.

peak_gpm.description: Peak hot-water flow (fixtures used at the same time) (gpm); default 4.5

name: calc_tankless_water_heater_size
title: Tankless Water Heater Size Calculator (GPM, Temperature Rise, BTU & kW)

description: How many bags of thin-set mortar to buy for your tile area and trowel notch, from manufacturer coverage per 50 lb bag, with a conservative and a best-case count. Formula: Bags = area × (1 + allowance) ÷ coverage per bag, rounded up, at the low and high ends of the coverage range. Data-sheet coverage per 50 lb bag: 1/4 × 1/4 in 80–95 sq ft, 1/4 × 3/8 in 60–70, 1/2 × 1/2 in 35–40 (scaled for other bag sizes).

coverage_sqft_per_bag.description: Coverage from your bag label (0 = use the data sheet) (sq ft); default 0

name: calc_thinset
title: Thinset Calculator (Bags of Thin-Set Mortar by Trowel Size)

description: Voltage drop for a single- or three-phase run using NEC Chapter 9 Table 8 conductor sizes. Formula: VD = 2 × K × I × L ÷ CM (single phase) or √3 × K × I × L ÷ CM (three phase); K = ohm·cmil/ft (approx. 12.9 Cu, 21.2 Al); CM from NEC Ch. 9 Table 8.

phase.description: Phase; default 1; one of 1 = Single phase, 3 = Three phase

name: calc_voltage_drop
title: Wire Size & Voltage Drop Calculator (AWG, Copper/Aluminum)

description: Studs at 16 or 24 in on center for a wall length, plus extras for corners and openings, and linear feet of top and bottom plate. Formula: Studs on layout = ⌈length(in) ÷ spacing⌉ + 1; total = layout + corners × extras per corner + openings × extras per opening. Plate linear ft = length × plates.

spacing_in.description: Stud spacing (on center); default 16; one of 16 = 16 in o.c., 24 = 24 in o.c., 12 = 12 in o.c.

name: calc_wall_stud
title: Wall Stud Calculator (Studs & Plates for a Framed Wall)

description: How big a water softener you need: grains of hardness removed per day from your household size and water hardness, the grain capacity for your regeneration interval, and how often a given softener will regenerate. Formula: Grains per day = people × gallons per person per day × hardness (gpg). Capacity needed = grains per day × days between regenerations. Days between regenerations = rated capacity ÷ grains per day. gpg = mg/L ÷ 17.1.

gal_per_person_day.description: Softened water per person per day (gal); default 75

rated_capacity_grains.description: Softener capacity from its spec sheet (optional) (grains); default 0

name: calc_water_softener_size
title: Water Softener Size Calculator (Grains per Day and Capacity)

description: What size well pressure tank you need: the drawdown for your pump's flow and minimum run time, the minimum total tank volume at your pressure-switch setting, and the smallest Amtrol Well-X-Trol model that delivers it. Formula: Required drawdown = pump gpm × run minutes. Acceptance factor = (cut-out − cut-in) ÷ (cut-out + 14.7). Minimum total tank volume = drawdown ÷ acceptance factor. A tank's drawdown = volume × acceptance factor (capped at its maximum acceptance factor). Run time = drawdown ÷ gpm.

cut_in_psi.description: Pressure switch cut-in; default 40; one of 20 = 20 psi, 30 = 30 psi, 40 = 40 psi, 50 = 50 psi, 60 = 60 psi

cut_out_psi.description: Pressure switch cut-out; default 60; one of 40 = 40 psi, 50 = 50 psi, 60 = 60 psi, 70 = 70 psi, 80 = 80 psi

run_minutes.description: Minimum pump run time; default 1; one of 1 = 1 minute (pumps up to 3/4 hp), 2 = 2 minutes (pumps over 3/4 hp)

name: calc_well_pressure_tank_size
title: Well Pressure Tank Size Calculator (Drawdown and Pump Run Time)

description: What gauge wire you need for a circuit: copper or aluminum size from the NEC ampacity table at the right temperature column, with the 125% continuous-load rule, the small-conductor breaker limits and an optional voltage-drop check for long runs. Formula: Design amps = load × 1.25 if continuous. Size = smallest AWG whose ampacity in the 60 °C (or 75 °C) column, capped by 240.4(D) for 14/12/10 AWG, is at least the design amps. Voltage drop % = 2 × K × I × L ÷ cmil ÷ V × 100 (√3 for three phase; K = 12.9 copper, 21.2 aluminum); step up until within the limit.

continuous.description: Continuous load (3 hours or more)?; default 1; one of 1 = Yes (size at 125%), 0 = No

one_way_ft.description: One-way length (0 = skip voltage drop) (ft); default 100

phase.description: Phase; default 1; one of 1 = Single phase, 3 = Three phase

terminal_c.description: Breaker/terminal rating; default 60; one of 60 = 60 °C (default for 100 A or less), 75 = 75 °C (listed equipment, or over 100 A)

name: calc_wire_size
title: Wire Size Calculator (Ampacity, 125% Rule and Voltage Drop)
